page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Rewrite using 1 + tan²x = sec²x and identify f(x), f′(x)
steps.why: The Pythagorean identity 1+tan²x=sec²x hides the f+f′ pairing until it is applied — once rewritten, the bracket is plainly tanx (f) plus sec²x (f′).
common_mistakes: Trying to match f and f′ in the ORIGINAL bracket 1+tan²x+tanx before applying the identity.
Misremembering the identity as 1+cot²x=sec²x instead of 1+tan²x=sec²x.
steps.memory_tip: 1+tan²x = sec²x — spot this identity FIRST whenever a bracket has a bare 1 next to a tan² term.

steps.label: Apply the formula for the final answer
steps.why: With f(x)=tanx identified, the standard eˣ[f+f′] result gives eˣtanx directly.
common_mistakes: Writing eˣ sec²x instead of eˣ tanx — the answer keeps f(x), not f′(x).
steps.memory_tip: The answer is eˣ times whichever term you called f(x) — here tanx, not sec²x.
